title: Satellite A velocity
description: Essential: Correctly states the linear velocity as v = sqrt(GM/R).

title: Satellite A period
description: Essential: Correctly states the orbital period as T' = sqrt(4π²R³/(GM)).

title: Satellite A acceleration
description: Essential: Correctly states the centripetal acceleration as a = GM/R².

title: Satellite B height
description: Essential: Correctly states the height above ground as h = cube_root(GMT²/(4π²)) - R.

title: Force balance reasoning
description: Important: Applies Newton's second law, setting gravitational force equal to centripetal force for a circular orbit.

title: Geostationary condition
description: Important: For part (2), identifies that the orbital period of satellite B must equal the Earth's rotation period T.

title: Orbital radius distinction
description: Important: Correctly uses R (Earth's radius) as the orbital radius for satellite A and R+h for satellite B.

title: Algebraic manipulation
description: Optional: Shows clear algebraic steps to solve for the required quantities from the force-balance equation.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Mentions or implies correct units for final answers (e.g., m/s, s, m/s², m).

title: Radius confusion error
description: Pitfall: Uses Earth's radius R as the orbital radius for the geostationary satellite, forgetting to add h.

title: Period confusion error
description: Pitfall: For part (2), uses the satellite A period formula instead of the Earth's rotation period T.
